key_insight: Editable conversation history can reduce context pollution by letting users revise past turns, keeping the model’s working state aligned with current intent.
engineering_relevance: For chat systems, mutable transcripts offer a practical UI/UX and state-management pattern to improve clarity, confidence, and continuity without forcing users to restart conversations.
method: Built a chat prototype that supports transcript-level edits via natural-language revision requests.
Compared mutable transcripts with standard chat in a controlled user study (n=17).
Analyzed representative transcripts to see how revisions affect conversation length and retained context.
evidence_signal: In the user study, participants significantly preferred mutable transcripts on clarity, confidence, and ease of use, and transcript analysis showed shorter conversations with obsolete context removed.
watch_item: This is an initial feasibility result with a small study; real-world deployment will need careful handling of edit history, consistency, and model behavior after transcript revisions.
paper_title: Mutable Transcripts: Mitigating Context Pollution through Editable Conversation State
